newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corn growers aim for $40 billion crop in 2002.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corn growers aim for $40 billion crop in 2002.

text.p: U.S. farmers aim to produce a $40 billion corn crop in the year 2002, boosted by sales of specialty corn and value-added corn oils, the head of the National Corn Growers Association said on Monday.
"It's an ambitious goal but we think we can do it," Wallie Hardie, president of the producers group, told Reuters in an interview at the U.S. Feed Grains Council meeting.
Last year, U.S. corn growers produced a 10 billion bushel crop valued at about $27 billion.
The $40 billion mark will be reached only by identifying new and higher value markets for corn, Hardie said.

"Our project for corn genome mapping will help us become more efficient," Hardie said. "And we need to differentiate our crop by producing higher quality starch or oil that can be used for industrial, chemical and pharmaceutical markets."
China, with its growing affluence and taste for grain-fed beef and poultry, is also expected to become a big buyer of U.S. corn during the coming five years, he said.

More U.S. corn farmers are also entering into contract production agreements with food processors to provide so-called "designer corn" intended for specific snack foods or other consumer goods, Hardie said.
